```{r scree-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 5,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE
)
```

This tutorial shows how to use `dp_scree()` to estimate private scree values and proportions of variance explained (PVE), inspect the results, and draw
scree and PVE plots. Also, it explains how to choose among the **clipped mean**, **private modified winsorized mean (PMWM)**, and **Huber mean** estimators.

The focus here is on **R arguments, control settings, and visualization**.
For the paired-difference construction, mathematical formulas, and privacy accounting, see [Theory of DP Scree](theory-dp-scree.html). 
For installation, example datasets, input requirements, and general privacy budget allocation, see [Getting Started](tutorials-getting-started.html).

## 1. Load the example data

We use `gau`, a synthetic dataset with 1,000 observations and 20 numeric variables. 
For more details, see the documentation for [`gau`](../reference/gau.html).

```{r scree-data}
library(dppca)
data("gau", package = "dppca")

X <- gau
dim(X)
```

## 2. Set the privacy budget and estimate scree values

Scree estimation needs a `loading` budget for private PC directions and a `scree` budget for the private variance estimator. 
When `split` is omitted,`dp_scree()` divides the total budget **equally** between these two components.

```{r scree-privacy}
scree_privacy <- privacy_control(
  eps = 6,
  delta = 1e-4
)
```

You can also specify a different allocation using `split` as explained in [Getting Started](tutorials-getting-started.html).

First, we use the clipped mean method to estimate scree values for the first five PCs:

```{r scree-fit}
set.seed(123)
scree_fit <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 5,
  privacy = scree_privacy,
  method = "clipped",
  control = clipped_control(C_clip = 20),
  non_private = TRUE
)

scree_fit
```

The `clipped_control()` function requires a public clipping threshold. The value `C_clip = 20` is an illustrative setting, not an automatic or universally recommended choice. 

The main arguments of `dp_scree()` are:

<style>
.scree-argument-table table {
  width: 100%;
  table-layout: fixed;
}
.scree-argument-table colgroup col:first-child {
  width: 18% !important;
}
.scree-argument-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) {
  width: 82% !important;
}
</style>

::: {.scree-argument-table}

| Argument | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `X` | Input observations, with numeric features in columns. |
| `k` | Number of leading PCs to estimate, from 1 to the number of numeric variables. |
| `privacy` | Total budget and loading/scree allocation from `privacy_control()`. |
| `method` | One or more of `"clipped"`, `"pmwm"`, and `"huber"` (default: `"clipped"`). |
| `control` | Method-specific tuning parameters, specified using `clipped_control()`, `pmwm_control()`, or `huber_control()`. |
| `cpp.option` | Use the compiled direction estimator (`TRUE`, the default) or its R implementation (`FALSE`). |
| `mono` | Enforce a nonincreasing scree sequence via isotonic regression (default: `TRUE`). |
| `non_private` | Compute an ordinary PCA comparison when `TRUE` (default: `FALSE`). |
| `V_dp` | Optionally reuse previously estimated private directions; their earlier loading budget must still be recorded. |

:::

## 3. Inspect and plot the result

Printing `scree_fit` shows a short overview of the fitted results. 
To see scree values, PVE, and cumulative PVE for each stored method, use `summary()`:

```{r scree-summary}
scree_summary <- summary(scree_fit)
scree_summary
```

The numeric estimates remain directly accessible by method. 
The optional ordinary PCA reference is under `nonprivate`, while data dimensions, selected methods, and privacy allocations are under `metadata`:

```{r scree-values}
scree_fit$clipped$scree
scree_fit$clipped$pve
scree_fit$nonprivate$scree
scree_fit$metadata$privacy
```

In a default private-only fit (`non_private = FALSE`), `scree_fit$nonprivate` is `NULL`; `scree_fit$clipped`, `$pmwm`, or `$huber` remain top-level method results. 

By default, `plot()` displays both the PVE and scree plots side by side. Because this example was fitted with `non_private = TRUE`, 
the ordinary PCA reference is included automatically; a fit with `non_private = FALSE` shows only private estimates:

```{r scree-default-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5, out.width="100%", results="hide", fig.alt="Private and ordinary PCA PVE and scree plots"}
plot(scree_fit)
```

To display only one view, use `type`. 

```{r scree-select-views, eval=FALSE}
plot(scree_fit, type = "pve")
plot(scree_fit, type = "scree")
```

<style>
.scree-plot-table table {
  width: 100%;
  table-layout: fixed;
}
.scree-plot-table colgroup col:first-child {
  width: 15% !important;
}
.scree-plot-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) {
  width: 85% !important;
}
</style>

::: {.scree-plot-table}

| Plot type | What it shows |
|:--|:--|
| `"pve"` | Each component's share of the estimated variation among the `k` fitted PCs. |
| `"scree"` | Estimated variation along each private PC direction, on its original scale. |
:::

## 4. Choose a method and its tuning parameters

The three scree estimators use the same projected paired differences, but differ in how they estimate their means. 
The tables below map the symbols used in [Theory of DP Scree](theory-dp-scree.html)** to the R arguments of each method-specific control function.

### Clipped mean {#clipped-control}

Clipped estimation limits each squared pair difference before releasing a noisy mean. See [Theory of Clipped mean](theory-dp-scree.html#clipped-mean).

<style>
.clipped-parameter-table table {width: 100%; table-layout: fixed;}
.clipped-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) {width: 20% !important;}
.clipped-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) {width: 20% !important;}
.clipped-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) {width: 60% !important;}
</style>

::: {.clipped-parameter-table}
| Theory notation | R argument | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $C_{\mathrm{clip}}$ | `C_clip` | Positive upper clipping threshold; controls the bias–noise tradeoff (required, no default). |
::: 

The setting used in Section 2 is:

```{r scree-clipped-control}
clipped_set <- clipped_control(C_clip = 20)
clipped_set
```

A smaller `C_clip` reduces sensitivity and Gaussian noise, but can truncate more large paired differences. 
A larger value reduces clipping bias while requiring more privacy noise.

### Private modified winsorized mean (PMWM) {#pmwm-control}

PMWM privately estimates lower and upper cutoffs and then computes a noisy winsorized mean. See [Theory of PMWM](theory-dp-scree.html#pmwm).

<style>
.pmwm-parameter-table table {width: 100%;table-layout: fixed;}
.pmwm-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) {width: 20% !important;}
.pmwm-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) {width: 20% !important;}
.pmwm-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) {width: 60% !important;}
</style>

::: {.pmwm-parameter-table}

| Theory notation | R argument | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $a,b$ | `a`, `b` | Public lower and upper bounds for the **estimated cutoffs**, with $a<b$ (required). |
| $c_{\mathrm{trim}}$ | `trim_const` | Positive baseline trimming constant in the quantile level (required). |
| $\eta_{\mathrm{trim}}$ | `eta` | Lower-bound tuning value for the trimming proportion, in $[0,0.5)$ (required). |
| $\beta$ | `beta` | Geometric quantile-search grid base, greater than 1 (default: `1.001`). |
| $I_Q,I_M$ | `split_mode` | `FALSE`: reuse all pair rows in both stages (default); `TRUE`: use disjoint quantile and mean subsets. |
:::

For example, to use PMWM instead of the clipped estimator:

```{r scree-pmwm}
pmwm_set <- pmwm_control(
  a = 0,
  b = 50,
  trim_const = 10,
  eta = 0.01
)
```

```{r scree-pmwm-fit, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
pmwm_fit <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 5,
  privacy = scree_privacy,
  method = "pmwm",
  control = pmwm_set,
  non_private = TRUE
)

summary(pmwm_fit)
plot(pmwm_fit, type = "pve")
```

### Huber mean {#huber-control}

The Huber method privately estimates a scale for each PC and uses thatscale to set a Huber threshold for noisy gradient descent. See [Huber mean theory](theory-dp-scree.html#huber-mean).

<style>
.huber-parameter-table table {width: 100%;table-layout: fixed;}
.huber-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) {width: 20% !important;}
.huber-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) {width: 20% !important;}
.huber-parameter-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) {width: 60% !important;}
</style>

::: {.huber-parameter-table}

| Theory notation | R argument | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $r_{\min},r_{\max}$ | `k_min_m2`, `k_max_m2` | Integer limits for the dyadic scale candidates $2^r$, with $r_{\min}<r_{\max}$ (required). |
| $\rho$ | `m2_frac` | Fraction of scree epsilon used for private scale estimation, in $(0,1)$ (required). |
| $\mu_0$ | `mu0` | Public initial mean iterate (default: `0`). |
| $\eta_0$ | `eta0` | Positive gradient-descent step size (default: `1`). |
| $T$ | `T` | Number of noisy gradient steps (default: `ceiling(log(m))`). |
| $M$ | `M` | Number of blocks for private scale estimation (default: `floor(sqrt(m / 2))`, capped by available pairs). |
:::

When `T` or `M` is left as `NULL`, the corresponding sample-size-based default is used. 

For example:

```{r scree-huber}
huber_set <- huber_control(
  k_min_m2 = -10,
  k_max_m2 = 10,
  m2_frac = 0.25
)
```

```{r scree-huber-fit, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
huber_fit <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 5,
  privacy = scree_privacy,
  method = "huber",
  control = huber_set,
  non_private = TRUE
)

summary(huber_fit)
plot(huber_fit, type = "pve")
```



## 5. Compare multiple methods and account for releases

To fit several methods using one private direction estimate, provide a vector of method names and a named list of their corresponding controls:

```{r scree-method-comparison}
set.seed(123)
scree_comparison <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 5,
  privacy = scree_privacy,
  method = c("clipped", "pmwm", "huber"),
  control = list(
    clipped = clipped_set,
    pmwm = pmwm_set,
    huber = huber_set
  ),
  non_private = TRUE
)

summary(scree_comparison)
```

```{r scree-method-comparison-plot, results="hide", fig.alt="PVE comparison of clipped, PMWM, Huber, and ordinary PCA"}
plot(scree_comparison, type = "pve")
```

Within a call, all methods share a single private direction estimate but independently compute their scree estimates using the full scree privacy budget. 


## 6. Reusing Private PC Directions {#reusing-private-pc-directions}

When supplying previously estimated directions through `V_dp`, specify the actual privacy budget used to estimate those directions as the `loading` allocation. 
This records the previously incurred privacy cost without spending the loading budget again.

There are two ways to specify the privacy allocation.

**Option 1: Specify component budgets directly.**

```{r scree-reuse-direct, eval=FALSE}
# Estimate private PC directions.
loading_fit <- dp_loading(
  X,
  eps = 3,
  delta = 5e-5
)

# Specify the actual loading budget and the scree budget.
reuse_privacy <- privacy_control(
  loading = c(eps = 3, delta = 5e-5),
  scree   = c(eps = 3, delta = 5e-5)
)
```

**Option 2: Specify a total budget and allocation proportions.**

```{r scree-reuse-split, eval=FALSE}
reuse_privacy <- privacy_control(
  eps = 6,
  delta = 1e-4,
  split = c(loading = 0.5, scree = 0.5)
)

# Estimate private PC directions using the allocated loading budget.
loading_budget <- reuse_privacy$components$loading

loading_fit <- dp_loading(
  X,
  eps = loading_budget[["eps"]],
  delta = loading_budget[["delta"]]
)
```

After either option, the estimated directions can be reused in `dp_scree()`:

```{r scree-reuse-directions, eval=FALSE}
scree_reused <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 5,
  privacy = reuse_privacy,
  method = "clipped",
  control = clipped_control(C_clip = 20),
  V_dp = loading_fit$directions,
  non_private = FALSE
)

summary(scree_reused)
```

## 7. Customize the plot

Use `scree_plot_control()` to change the appearance of the stored plot.

```{r scree-custom-plot, results="hide", fig.alt="Customized PVE plot comparing private and ordinary PCA"}
plot(
  scree_fit,
  type = "pve",
  plot_control = scree_plot_control(
    title = "PVE among the first five PCs",
    col = c(nonprivate = "grey30", clipped = "#1F4E79"),
    legend_labels = c(nonprivate = "Ordinary PCA", clipped = "Clipped DP"),
    lwd = 2,
    point_cex = 1.2,
    cex_main = 1.2,
    legend_position = "topright"
  )
)
```

| Setting | What it changes |
|:--|:--|
| `title`, `xlab`, `ylab` | Plot title and axis labels. |
| `col`, `lty`, `pch` | Named series colors, line types, and point symbols. |
| `lwd`, `point_cex` | Line width and point-size multiplier. |
| `cex_main`, `cex_lab`, `cex_axis` | Title, axis-label, and tick-label sizes. |
| `legend_position`, `legend_labels`, `cex_legend`, `legend_bty` | Legend position, labels, size, and border. |


For complete argument descriptions, see `?dp_scree`, `?plot.dp_scree`, and `?scree_plot_control`.
